symptoms: Brief knocking or rattling after a cold start
operating_conditions: First start after an overnight stop
diagnostic_steps: Document how long the noise lasts and arrange professional diagnosis
expert_insight: Synthetic example: the duration and temperature dependence of a noise provide useful diagnostic context.
common_mistakes: Treating all cold-start noises as the same fault
safety_precautions: Stop the engine if oil-pressure warnings persist; seek qualified inspection

diagnostic_steps: Record driving conditions and warning indications for a qualified mechanic
expert_insight: Synthetic example: compare when the temperature rises, rather than assuming one component is responsible.
common_mistakes: Continuing to drive with a temperature warning
safety_precautions: Stop safely and switch off the engine when overheating
Never open a hot cooling system

diagnostic_steps: Record whether symptoms change between cold and warm operation
Have diagnostic fault codes assessed by a qualified mechanic
expert_insight: Synthetic example: stored codes are clues and do not alone confirm a failed component.
common_mistakes: Replacing components solely from a fault-code description
safety_precautions: Do not run the engine in an enclosed space
Seek inspection for a flashing engine warning light

diagnostic_steps: Record whether the engine cranks during a failed start
Note dashboard indications and arrange inspection
expert_insight: Synthetic example: distinguishing no-crank from crank-but-no-start narrows the investigation.
common_mistakes: Using the phrase will not start without recording whether the engine cranks
safety_precautions: Do not bypass starter circuits or safety interlocks

symptoms: Vibration felt through the vehicle body
diagnostic_steps: Document the engine speed and operating conditions where vibration occurs
expert_insight: Synthetic example: record whether vibration follows engine speed or vehicle road speed.
common_mistakes: Assuming every vibration is caused by an engine mount
safety_precautions: Keep clear of moving belts and fans
Have severe or new vibration professionally inspected

diagnostic_steps: Compare actual fuel used and distance travelled under similar conditions
Record warning lights for professional assessment
expert_insight: Synthetic example: a consistent measurement baseline helps distinguish a fault from changes in use.
common_mistakes: Diagnosing excessive consumption only from the dashboard range estimate
safety_precautions: Stop safely and seek assistance if fuel is leaking or a strong fuel smell occurs

diagnostic_steps: Record warning lights, engine temperature and when power is lost
expert_insight: Synthetic example: describe load and temperature conditions before clearing fault information.
common_mistakes: Clearing diagnostic codes before recording them
safety_precautions: Avoid driving if loss of power makes traffic manoeuvres unsafe

diagnostic_steps: Record the position and appearance of the leak without going beneath an unsupported vehicle
expert_insight: Synthetic example: airflow and gravity can move oil away from the original leak point.
common_mistakes: Assuming the lowest visible oil spot is the origin of the leak
safety_precautions: Do not drive with an oil pressure warning
Never work under a vehicle supported only by a jack

diagnostic_steps: Record smoke colour, temperature conditions and duration for professional assessment
expert_insight: Synthetic example: smoke appearance alone is insufficient to confirm an internal engine fault.
common_mistakes: Confusing brief cold-weather condensation with a confirmed coolant leak
safety_precautions: Seek qualified inspection for persistent smoke or fluid loss

diagnostic_steps: Record temperature, dashboard indications and whether restarting is possible
expert_insight: Synthetic example: recording conditions at the moment of failure is valuable when a fault is intermittent.
common_mistakes: Assuming an intermittent fault is repaired because the engine restarts
safety_precautions: Unexpected shutdown can reduce steering and brake assistance; stop safely and seek recovery assistance
